title: release.yml: evaluate lore/quest version parity on every dispatch, not only publish:true
description: Found 2026-09-27 answering quest-cli's QCLI-386 AC4 ("the mechanism matches what lore-cli built"). lore's Article 3.6 parity step (scripts/version-parity.mjs --require) sits inside release.yml's publish job, whose job-level if: inputs.publish == true skips the whole job on a publish:false dispatch, so a dry-run dispatch never evaluates parity and can go green on a mismatched lore/quest pair. quest-cli's release.yml evaluates its parity step on dry dispatches too. Not a safety hole (publish:false publishes nothing, and publish-release.sh --dry-run already runs parity), but a mismatch should surface on the dry dispatch before a real release. opum-agent ruling 2026-09-27 (cross-session): fix now, reviewer pass, reference OPAG-465 AC1 and QCLI-386. The rule itself (checkVersionParity, the peer ref, fail-closed) does not change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml evaluates scripts/version-parity.mjs --require on every workflow_dispatch, publish:true and publish:false alike, in a job with no inputs.publish condition
The publish job cannot start unless that parity evaluation succeeded, and still refuses publication on a mismatch and fails closed on an unreadable quest-cli ref

test/release-workflow.test.ts pins the every-dispatch job, its lack of an inputs.publish guard, and publish depending on it; the pin goes red when the job is guarded by inputs.publish again (mutation shown)
The gate is proven both ways by running the checker the new job runs: a matched pair passes (exit 0) and a mismatched pair refuses (exit 1), recorded on this task with output
Reviewer pass on the release.yml change before it lands

plan: Add a release.yml job that runs scripts/version-parity.mjs --require on every dispatch (no inputs.publish condition), sparse-checking out only /package.json and /scripts/version-parity.mjs, no persisted credentials

Add it to publish's needs so publish cannot start without it; keep publish's own in-job parity step as the re-check nearest npm publish (the qualification jobs between can run long, and quest-cli main can move)
Pin both in test/release-workflow.test.ts; mutation: re-add if: inputs.publish == true to the new job and expect red
Prove the checker both ways (match exit 0, mismatch exit 1); reviewer pass; PR into dev; close in the delivering PR; promote
